context.body: Communities, suffering, and final charge · 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18
context.label: Communities, suffering, and final charge

observations.body: Grief is answered with resurrection and gathering. But we don’t want you to be ignorant, brothers, about those who have fallen asleep, so that you don’t grieve like the rest, who have no hope. Therefore comfort one another with these words.
observations.label: Grief is answered with resurrection and gathering

observations.body: The passage presents Grief is answered with resurrection and gathering as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Grief is answered with resurrection and gathering

observations.body: The passage places God beside Grief is answered with resurrection and gathering.
observations.label: God

payload.posture: Read 1 Thessalonians 4:13–18 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states grief is answered with resurrection and gathering. But we don’t want you to be ignorant, brothers, about those who have fallen asleep, so that you don’t grieve like the rest, who have no hope. Therefore comfort one another with these words. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
payload.title: Grief is answered with resurrection and gathering
